notes.title: "Fun with Objects, Part 1" is out NOW!
notes.notes: [p]Great news, everyone! It’s taken us forever, but we’re finally able to tell you the first part of the Fun with Objects Update is now [b]live on Steam[/b]![/p][p]Why only the first part? The demand for multi-level maps and roofs has been enormous over the last years, and we wanted to give our users the possibility to use both. This meant that all assets in Dungeon Alchemist needed to be reconfigured to adapt to the new height requirements, and, more importantly, that we had to come up with a sound way to generate roofs on any given shape of room you may come up with. [b]The algorithm for this simply didn’t exist. [/b]We had to write it ourselves. No easy task given the insane complexity, and it took a long time to get it absolutely right.[/p][p]To bring you the features we promised in the Fun with Objects update, we then had a choice: develop those extra features, and delay the update for several more months, or give you access to the current features, and add the remaining ones over the next update. We chose the latter, which brings us where we are now. The next part will not be nearly as fundamental as this one, so we’re confident we can release much sooner. And that part will contain most of the object-related improvements.[/p][p]But we managed to cram quite a few long-requested in this update as well, so check out the trailer below for an overview.[/p][p][/p][previewyoutube="Rw4osh9UoYU;full"][/previewyoutube][p][/p][p]So, without further ado: What are those new features?[/p][p][/p][h1]Multi-level Buildings[/h1][p]First off: Multi-level! You can now draw any room anywhere, and move up or down a floor with the menu on the right side, or the + and - key on your keypad. This will allow you to draw another room right on top or below. And another one. We didn’t cap the amount of rooms you can stack on top of each other. Yet. 🙂[/p][p]You can choose to build a regular room on top of another and remove the floors between them to create a higher room: perfect for a cathedral. Columns will automatically adapt to the new heightened ceiling. If you want to change the style of a roof, you can easily do so with the new Roof Menu in the left sidebar.[/p][p]The multi-level thing also brought a fundamental change to the stairs: they now connect automatically between floors, and remove the floor in the room above. They’re not as flexible as before, but that is something we’ll try to address in the next update. Hatches, pits and holes also received a complete makeover for them to function correctly in this update. [/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40663413/004d34e2beed7cb437ce1e74e1b823bdb7378c2f.jpg"][/img][/p][h1]Underground Terrain[/h1][p]Going up was the easy part, and to enable you to go down we needed to provide you with an underground terrain. That terrain had to accommodate rooms above ground at different heights, rooms below ground at various depths, and an editable terrain for you to make caves.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40663413/dd941eaf808a58a4aaec25beda6b69c93d9ca790.jpg"][/img][/p][h1]Realistic Interior Lighting[/h1][p]This one has been requested from the very start: a way to [b]hide the sun from shining over the walls[/b] inside rooms. Because we added roofs, this was now possible to implement, and you can toggle this on in the Settings menu. You can now finally have realistic indoor lighting![/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40663413/5447538c02be1f4ddad207279cae7f43fe5eea95.jpg"][/img][/p][h1]Abstract Lights[/h1][p]You can now place Abstract Lights in your scene. These are invisible lights that are not exported, but can be used to improve the lighting. Please use them sparingly, as they can be cause performance issues when you place a lot of them.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40663413/041b4c91c99e3275d03de73f449bbd5789d6f19b.jpg"][/img][/p][h1]Object Improvements[/h1][p]We didn’t abandon the Fun with Objects theme completely, by the way: this update contains the the following improvements related to having actual fun with objects:[/p][list][*][p]Added a new tab to the object menu that will only appear when certain objects are selected. This [b]Modular Objects Menu[/b] allows you to easily select related objects, and will also allow you to easily connect these objects together with a new UI. Currently, this is only used for [b]rails, pipes and the alchemical pipes[/b], but this will be extended in the future to allow you, for example, to build modular ships (spoiler alert!)[/p][/*][/list][list][*][p]Added a [b]Custom Objects Brush[/b], allowing you to turn any object into a brush. You can access this feature from the "Paint Objects" tab in the Objects menu.[/p][/*][*][p]Added a [b]global scale modifier[/b] for objects to its advanced menu in the top right.[/p][/*][*][p]As usual, there’s a [b]ton of new assets[/b] for you to play around with. notes.title: Fun with Objects - Release Announcement
notes.notes:
Hi everyone,

We know you’re all anxiously awaiting the [b]Fun with Objects[/b] update. We wanted to let you know that, after careful deliberation, we’ve decided to break this update into two parts.
Everything in Dungeon Alchemist has received such a massive overhaul that developing and testing all the features in this update would push the release further than we’d like. So, in order to get these features to all of you as soon as possible, [b]we’re splitting the update[/b] and are hoping to [b]release the first part early July this year[/b].

The first part of the update will contain the (literal) ground works: multi-level buildings, roofs, .. The second part will deliver on more specific Fun with Objects features, like full 3D rotation and multi-object selection.

You’ll notice in the first part that Dungeon Alchemist has changed drastically: maps are no longer limited to one level, and you’ll be able to freely create buildings at multiple levels (even underground!). We’ve also given you more control over lighting, with the introduction of abstract lights (lights from an invisible source), and all AI’s have received a massive overhaul.

You might wonder why this update is taking so long. Ever since we started Dungeon Alchemist people have been asking for roofs over their buildings. A fair request, and something we’ve been meaning to tackle for a long time. This seemed as good a time as any to start.

One of the first things we noticed about roofs is that they are not rooms: it’s perfectly possible to create any given shape between two floors that is neither the room above or the room below. Check out the image below for an example of how weird these shapes can get.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40663413/159c407b33b970d5ac9b72bc631cc4861197ef82.jpg[/img]
[i]An example of the strange shapes a roof could take[/i]

To fix this issue, we needed to write a new roof border system, that can create borders of any given size and fill odd shapes seamlessly. That finished, it became clear that it was very easy to mistake those flat roofs and roof borders for regular rooms. Not being able to manipulate them in the same way we’re used to felt off and buggy. There was the added issue that our flat roofs did not look very roof-like, further confusing everyone.

We needed a way to clearly distinguish our roofs from our rooms system, and the most straightforward way was to finally tackle the thing we’ve been dreading from the start: slanted roofs.

Not just slanted roofs, but slanted roofs auto-generated over any given stupidly impossible shape. That’s where we ventured into unexplored development territory. There was no algorithm available on earth that accurately covered all our use cases. So we had to develop one. The good news: we did. Dungeon Alchemist is now capable of generating any given themed roof in milliseconds. [b]This is absolutely groundbreaking[/b], and we are not aware of any other software that does this. The bad news, of course, is that getting this to work took us far longer than initially expected. 

There is a vast amount of features related to Fun with Objects that we’re actively developing, but it seemed unfair to make everyone wait until we’ve finalized those, too. So we’re splitting the update. We’re confident there’s more than enough new content in this first part for you to enjoy this completely new approach to making maps. Once more, I’d like to thank all of you for your patience, and I truly hope this first part of the Fun with Objects will exceed your expectations of what Dungeon Alchemist can be.

To demonstrate the flexibility of the new multilevel system, we have added a few screenshots to this announcement  to showcase what you'll be able to do… soon!

notes.title: Fun With Objects – Dev News
notes.notes:
We know you anxiously await our next big update, “Fun with Objects.” Because this is such a massive and game-changing update, we wanted to take a moment to give a brief heads-up on work in progress and what we’re actually working on behind the scenes, so to speak. It’s shaping up to be one of our most significant and exciting updates yet! 

Here are some teasers of some of the new features we planned, below: 

[h3]Multi-level Room Generation! 🏗️[/h3]
We’re taking Dungeon Alchemist⚗️ to the next level, literally. It will be possible to create and add multiple floors to your buildings, and build any room on top of any other room. And yes, this will bring roofs and ceilings, too.

[previewyoutube=bmjxo-5lFuw;full][/previewyoutube]

[previewyoutube=521H_XpFyCY;full][/previewyoutube]

[previewyoutube=Xr85Ernjj9c;full][/previewyoutube]

[h3]Going underground ⛏️[/h3]
Seeing as we’re going up, we figured we may as well start going down. In the Fun with Objects update it will be possible to go below the level of the current terrain, and even manipulate the terrain below the surface. 

[previewyoutube=UqBg4QtAOQI;full][/previewyoutube]
[previewyoutube=GqO0hBAveog;full][/previewyoutube]

[h3]Custom Object Brushes 🎨[/h3]
We’ll be making it possible to turn any object into a brush, so you can easily plop down a massive amount of just about anything, including custom objects from the Steam Workshop.

[previewyoutube=GZa2T89Fqy0;full][/previewyoutube]

[h3]Universal Object Scaling 📏[/h3]
This quality-of-life feature allows you to change the scale of your entire object collection. Whether you're making a tiny village or a castle for giants, the object's size will now match your vision.

[previewyoutube=PTfSmo07v0M;full][/previewyoutube]

[h3]Abstract Lighting (Invisible light sources) 💡[/h3]
Fun with Objects will feature new, easily placed, and adjusted light sources that disappear on export to properly light any scene in seconds. 

[previewyoutube=-hvmYUYp87Q;full][/previewyoutube]

[h3]Batch Map Exports 🗺️[/h3]
We’re designing a robust feature to output any number of maps easily, and with different export settings. 

[previewyoutube=vlOjUpXbdHI;full][/previewyoutube]

[h3]Decals – A tool to paint overlays on just about anything 🖌️[/h3]
Ever wanted to put moss on everything? Or graffiti on a roll of bread? Now you can!

[previewyoutube=1dhM225Q960;full][/previewyoutube]

Furthermore:
[list]
[*] Object rotation on any axis
[*] The ability to save any group of objects as a variant
[*] Modular assets to allow for the easy creation of complex structures
[/list]
… and a lot more!

All of these are game-changing additions, and they forced us to basically rebuild Dungeon Alchemist from the ground up. That takes time, and we truly appreciate your patience. More information and teasers will become available as soon as we can share them. If you have any questions or feedback, please do not hesitate to comment below. We are still entirely committed to making Dungeon Alchemist the absolute best it can be. We have listened to your feedback, and in the future we will try our best to provide a monthly development update. In the mean, for daily news, questions, and support, don't hesitate to [url=https://discord.gg/npHsUxuk]join our Discord[/url]!

Thank you all for your support of Dungeon Alchemist⚗️. We couldn’t have done all this without you!

notes.title: The "Magic" Update: is Live!
notes.notes:
Hello everyone! This update has taken longer than usual, but with good reason: we've listened to your requests and have finally taken the plunge to implement [b]curved/diagonal[/b] walls and [b]raised/rotated rooms[/b]!

This is by far the biggest update in Dungeon Alchemist yet and required a considerable part of our codebase to be rewritten. This also means that Dungeon Alchemist might be a bit less stable in the coming weeks. We'll be working hard at addressing any issues that pop up, but it is expected that more crashes and bugs will occur than usual after an update. Please bear with us as we take care of them.

But we absolutely believe the end result is worth it: you can make your maps so much more organic, dynamic and varied with these new features! We've also added a new biome, lots of new assets and a ton of new features for you to enjoy. Check it out in the trailer below!

[previewyoutube=XKJpW3s4BR8;full][/previewyoutube]
Let's go over the major changes in this update.


[h1]Curved/diagonal Walls[/h1]

The showstopper here is, of course, the curved walls. You can now change the shape of a room you're drawing by dragging the little circles to create convex, concave or diagonal shapes. It's intuitive, powerful, fast and fun!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40663413/9ba52cf2a38a78152fbc7fc556e9063537b1de10.jpg[/img]
[i]Wizards really love curves[/i]


[h1]Raised/rotated Rooms[/h1]

We also added the feature to rotate/raise rooms, allowing you to make little hamlets built on a mountainside or a layered castle with different height levels.

This does not mean you can make multi-level buildings just yet, though! The rooms still have to be placed separately on the horizontal plane, but adding the raised/rotated room feature was a necessary preparation step for implementing multi-level buildings. More on this later.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40663413/3d9386ef2f07a20ac974a498248f56302c54162c.jpg[/img]
[i]Finally. A real castle![/i]

[h1]Improved Object Brushes[/h1]

We have upgraded the options for object brushes, allowing you to draw grids, lines and circles easily. We even unlocked advanced settings so you can fine-tune the behavior to the smallest detail.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40663413/f76a8ac61416e146c200b5cbf16ef55b2902390f.jpg[/img]


[h1]New Fey Biome[/h1]

The new fey biome sports some really exotic plant species and will definitely spice up your campaign. Explore the mushroom forest, the crystal plane or the fey jungle... but don't get lost!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40663413/97fe33d36510c6ca564ee7b7c9ca8ced8036be7d.jpg[/img]


[h1]600+ Assets[/h1]

As usual, we've added several new room themes, including the Skeletal Throne Room, Village Cathedral, Potion Class, Extradimensional Room and Witch's Hut.

We've also added 600+ new assets including a few really funky ones that will surprise and delight your players. Confront them with the Wandering Hut, Flesh Chest, Eyed Abomination, Aetherial Loom or Death's Door, and see how they react!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40663413/500944b425bd22c902e37eae509cf222ec1c7140.jpg[/img]
[i]There's also this... thing.[/i]


[h1]New Tokens![/h1]

We've partnered with [url=https://www.bitethebulletstudio.com/]Bite The Bullet[/url] to bring new tokens to Dungeon Alchemist! This update features a pack of 23 magic-themed tokens, including this super-friendly Lord of Bones.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40663413/f4a188b991d06f915b6d62098cbd0c9f02eca72e.jpg[/img]
[i]Skeletons have feelings too.[/i]


[h1]Free Demo Version[/h1]

If you're still on the fence about Dungeon Alchemist, let them try out our demo! It's available right now, and features the Tavern theme alongside all objects contained within the tavern.


[h1]Other Improvements[/h1]

[list]
[*]Automatically add buttons to enable/disable animations and lights on models downloaded from the Steam Workshop.
[*]Added "Remove Water" brush to the terrain brushes.
[*]Added undo/redo support when drawing new rooms.
[*]Added optional autosave option (enable it in the Settings menu).
[*]Added green screen background option for those streamers with exotic setups (looking at you Mac).
[*]Added a calendar to the Cartomancer Chronicles to highlight upcoming community events and streams.
[*]Added icon to indicate whether an object was downloaded from the Steam Workshop or not.
[*]Added a "no borders" option to the export.
[*]Considerably sped up the application for users who have uploaded or downloaded a lot of assets from the Steam Workshop.
[/list]


[h1]What's Next?[/h1]

[b]Multi-level buildings, that's what's next[/b]! With all prerequisites in place, we're finally ready to take Dungeon Alchemist to the next level and allow you to place one room on top of an existing one. Something to look forward to in our next update: "Fun With Objects"!

In the meantime, we're looking forward to seeing all the crazy stuff you'll be building with the new room features! Enjoy!

notes.title: The "Treasury" Update is Live!
notes.notes:
It's time to embark on another adventure, because vast new riches have arrived from foreign shores, and someone REALLY needs to go loot them. The Treasury update brings tons of new, shiny, sparkling things for you to toy with, but also multiple other new features and improvements. Check out the trailer below: 

[previewyoutube=hSoCQbtLpjM;full][/previewyoutube]

Let's go over the biggest changes in this update.


[h1]Custom Asset Importer[/h1]
The Treasury update ships with a [b]custom asset importer[/b], allowing you all to import and [b]configure your own 3D models[/b]. If you're a 3D modeller and you have some models lying around that you would like to import, [url=https://dungeonalchemist.fandom.com/wiki/Asset_Importer]read this guide[/url] for more info on how to do this.

We currently only have an elaborate guide for [url=https://dungeonalchemist.fandom.com/wiki/Exporting_an_Asset_to_Dungeon_Alchemist#Blender_Export_Guide]Blender[/url], so if you use another 3D modelling program, feel free to expand [url=https://dungeonalchemist.fandom.com/wiki/DungeonAlchemist_Wiki]The Wiki[/url] with a guide for your tool of choice.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40663413/219b10dadd879031a232df377f00b3310a9eeba7.jpg[/img][i]You can now configure your own assets![/i]
 
And once the models are imported and configured, you can easily share them on the [b]Steam Workshop[/b], so other people can use them! This opens up a whole new world of possibilities for Dungeon Alchemist, as you're no longer limited to the assets we provide.
 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40663413/d76c929d9c09cce22b3f9f30699b6da707a5371b.jpg[/img][i]Share your assets with the world[/i]
 

[h1]600+ New Assets[/h1]
This update ships with a whopping [b]600+ new assets[/b]. These include of course tons of treasures, but also an absurd amount of foodstuffs, a greenhouse, a magic lantern, a foreboding necrotic gate and a harp. As usual, you can check out all the new assets from the different New categories found in the object menus.
 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40663413/7fcfd880da007037f51838ac8b2f25780eb70629.jpg[/img][i]Money money money![/i]
 

[h1]Overlays & Trace Images[/h1]
We added an overlay menu that allows you to place [b]labels[/b], [b]frames[/b] and other things on top of your map. It's a fun new way to bring your map to the next level and give it a bit of a personal touch.
 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40663413/78d5b67de3722a3d23cb33815b0f20e0b68e5dcd.jpg[/img][i]Muki's bakery, now with labels[/i]
 
Additionally, you can also configure a [b]trace image[/b] here that will be overlaid transparently on top of your map, allowing you to use this image as a template to model your dungeon on. This is a quick and easy way to [b]remake a battlemap[/b] you downloaded in Dungeon Alchemist!
 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40663413/2f36ad86b61f4a2e8c347443a8dc2de2d63a272a.jpg[/img][i]Trace overlays allow you to recreate battlemaps in Dungeon Alchemist[/i]
 

[h1]Openable Chests & Cupboards[/h1]
A selection of objects such as [b]chests[/b] and [b]cupboards[/b] can now be opened and closed, and you can even put stuff inside of them! And close them again! And move them around with its content inside! Wow!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40663413/fb8300bf900743b631ea815123aa6bf86f796fac.png[/img]
 

[h1]Support for AboveVTT & Fantasy Grounds Video[/h1]

As we want to support as many VTTs as possible, we have improved our export functionality:
[list]
[*] Added support for [url=https://chrome.google.com/webstore/detail/abovevtt/ipcjcbhpofedihcloggaichibomadlei]AboveVTT [/url]
[*] Added support for video export for Fantasy Grounds
[/list]


[h1]Quality-of-life Improvements[/h1]

As usual, we also added a bunch of quality-of-life improvements:

[list]
[*] You can now [b]scale objects infinitely[/b] by turning [b]collisions off[/b] in the object menu. The era of "place max scaled object on other object and scale that one" is finally over.
[*] When starting Dungeon Alchemist, [b]the last OPENED map will now be re-opened[/b] automatically instead of the last SAVED map.
[*] Show a warning when opening a map from the workshop when you have [b]unsaved changes[/b].
[*] Added [b]scrollbar[/b] to the object menu. Hooray!
[*] Added a hotkey ([b]Ctrl+Shift+X[/b]) for the Erase Objects functionality.
[*] Added warnings for when you try to export an image/video for Foundry if Foundry does not support an image/video that large.
[/list]


[h1]What's Next?[/h1]

Dungeon Alchemist remains a work-in-progress, and we will keep on implementing new features from the Kickstarter stretch goals, and more! If you want to be the first to know what's coming up, [url=https://discord.com/invite/Gqa2EtvTva]join our Discord[/url], as we'll be posting teasers there as soon as we're ready.

Until then, enjoy your gold, treasures, labels, frames and custom assets, and be sure to submit your map for the next [url=https://dungeonalchemist.fandom.com/wiki/.DAM_Challenge].DAM Challenge[/url] for a chance to get featured in the Cartomancer Chronicles.

Stay tuned for the next chapter in the Dungeon Alchemist adventure: "Magic"!

[i]Yours in Cartomancy,

The Dungeon Alchemist Team[/i]

notes.title: The "Everything is Lava" Update is Live!
notes.notes:
Hi everyone!

With winter (almost) behind us, it's time to focus on the future, and as you all know, the future is [b]SCORCHING HOT[/b]! And our "Everything Is Lava" update is here to bring that heat to your next roleplaying campaign!

This update comes with [b]two new terrain types[/b] ([b]Caves and Skeletal Plains[/b]), [b]hundreds of new objects[/b], [b]free vertical movement[/b], [b]pits[/b], [b]a newspaper[/b] and much, much more.

Check out the trailer below for an overview:

[previewyoutube=VU7f9ZOBUQ0;full][/previewyoutube]


[h1]Caves & Skeletal Plains[/h1]

The biggest feature of this update is the long-awaited addition of [b]caves[/b]! For starters, we added a dedicated cave biome, along with multiple elevation settings such as [b]labyrinth[/b], [b]burrow[/b], [b]ridge[/b] and [b]tunnel[/b], as well as multiple vegetation settings such as [b]glowing mushrooms[/b] and [b]crystals[/b].

But we didn't stop there! We also added cave support to all existing terrain types! You can go to the Cave Tab in the terrain menu and [b]draw a cave area on any terrain[/b]. This will raise the terrain to max level and will allow you to carve a cave out of this area. This allows you to make a forest with a small cave on the side, for example.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40663413/4e9d6cc8d273c750bde086f89b7297cc427f432f.jpg[/img]
[i]A cave in the snow terrain type[/i]
 
Finally, as a bonus, we also added a new Skeletal Plains terrain type:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40663413/d533d9740cfb53d0f04e974d9a67bf3fa2e084a5.jpg[/img]
[i]Someone took a wrong turn[/i]


[h1]Organic Rooms[/h1]

Organic rooms are a [b]new AI room type[/b] that is used by default in the Caves terrain type, but can also be used in other terrain types.

Organic rooms will [b]not spawn any walls or floors[/b], and will [b]follow the shape of the terrain[/b]. They will not flatten the terrain, and will place objects against natural walls such as the walls of the cave or the edge of a ravine.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40663413/1c2deea95b8744c0d4363a8252ec71fbef945631.jpg[/img]
[i]An organic dissection room in a cave[/i]
 

[h1]Cartomancer Chronicles - a Dungeon Alchemist Newspaper![/h1]

When we launched our Steam Workshop, we would never have guessed that so many people would start uploading incredible creations. With [b]almost 3k maps uploaded[/b] after half a year, it gets increasingly harder for new maps to get noticed.

That's why we launched the [b]Cartomancer Chronicles[/b], a newspaper for Dungeon Alchemist that will put a spotlight on community creations that deserve it. Every week, we'll handpick our favourite new map of the week and let people know about it. We'll also feature the [url=https://dungeonalchemist.fandom.com/wiki/.DAM_Challenge].DAM challenge[/url] in the newspaper. Finally, it'll also contain tips & tricks, announcements of any kind and other cool stuff! A new edition will be released [b]every Monday[/b], and you can read it [b]right from within Dungeon Alchemist[/b]!

Be sure to press that [b]Like Button[/b] below the map of the week to show your support for the incredible efforts of our community!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40663413/6dc8c79d144a5835c87887825a4b6bc591ed4fa8.jpg[/img]
 

[h1]Pits[/h1]

We added a new room type called pits to Dungeon Alchemist. Pits are rooms that lie below zero and that allow you to add some height differences to your maps until we add full-fledged support for rooms on multiple levels.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40663413/1e5993e80ba68ece8c268019ff41b568d2f3b9e7.jpg[/img]
[i]A small hamlet with a canal flowing through[/i]


[h1]Quality-of-life Improvements[/h1]

As usual, we added several quality-of-life improvements, some eagerly awaited by a lot of our users:
[list]

[*]You can now [b]override the vertical position of any object[/b] by turning collisions off in the object menu and then using the vertical arrow to place the object on any height. Ultimate freedom of movement is finally at your fingertips!
[*]You can copy & paste the configured properties of an object (for example, light color or open/closed door) by selecting it and clicking [b]Edit > Copy Object Properties[/b] or hitting [b]Ctrl+C[/b]. You can then paste these properties in a wide area, which will result in all objects getting the same settings. No more turning off all lights manually!
[*]Bridges, huts and other large objects will now level the terrain and remove objects below them, making them much easier to place. You no longer have to painstakingly match the terrain height on either side of the bridge, as we'll do it automatically for you.
[*]Some objects such as the new rails and pipes will now [b]snap to each other[/b], making it very easy to construct connected rail paths or sewers. Some older objects such as the modular bridge parts will do this as well!
[*]Added functionality to easily [b]hide the grid[/b] from the View Menu.
[*]Added functionality to [b]disable all nature animations[/b] from the View Menu.
[/list]


[h1]A Wiki![/h1]

We created [url=https://dungeonalchemist.fandom.com/wiki/DungeonAlchemist_Wiki]a Wiki[/url] to collect info and know-how about Dungeon Alchemist. Our goal is to make it the go-to place for any info about Dungeon Alchemist, including lesser-known functionality and tips & tricks. Until now, most of this has been shared on [url=https://discord.com/invite/Wrrmb5YrJa]our Discord[/url], but not everyone uses Discord and we want to share this knowledge with our wider community.

Wiki's are a community effort, so we will not be building all of it on our own - [b]we're counting on industrious fans to give us a helping hand![/b] If you feel up for it, go ahead and [url=https://dungeonalchemist.fandom.com/wiki/DungeonAlchemist_Wiki]expand the wiki[/url] with anything you might know about our app.


[h1]What's next?[/h1]

This update came much faster than the previous one, and this was because a lot of the effort was already done behind the scenes during the development of the Winter Wonderland update. We're very happy that we can finally say that one of the most-requested features from the start (caves) is now properly supported by our app.

But what's next? We still have a bunch of stretch goals to finish. If you want to be the first to know what's coming up, [url=https://discord.gg/Wrrmb5YrJa]join our Discord[/url], as we'll be posting teasers there as soon as we're ready.

Until then, enjoy your caves and skeletal plains, and be sure to submit your map for the next [url=https://dungeonalchemist.fandom.com/wiki/.DAM_Challenge].DAM Challenge[/url] for a chance to get featured in the Cartomancer Chronicles! 

[i]Yours in Cartomancy,
The Dungeon Alchemist Team[/i]

notes.title: The Winter Wonderland Update is live!
notes.notes:
Hello everyone!

We've just launched the [b]Winter Wonderland update[/b] to all our users. Whether you want to trek across vast ice fields in the north, scale snowy mountaintops or explore that haunted forest that suddenly froze overnight: we've got you covered!

The Winter Wonderland update comes with a new [b]snow terrain type[/b], a [b]snow weather effect[/b] that can be applied to all your existing maps, [b]584 new objects[/b], a [b]video export[/b] feature, [b]special effects[/b] and tons of other quality-of-life improvements. As a bonus, we overhauled the entire AI to produce much, [i]much[/i] better results. We'll walk you through them in this update, but first: the trailer!

[previewyoutube=cGkMIggInzE;full][INSERT TRAILER][/previewyoutube]


[h1]Snow Terrain[/h1]

You can now pick "snow" as a terrain type when creating your map. But that is not all: you can also add a snow overlay to any map you create. The snow overlay will cover any outside objects in a thick layer of snow, for that ultimate winter look! You can even apply the snow effect to your existing maps!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40663413/f33088a83ea54bfbb7af89605e626ffb019855c5.jpg[/img]


[h1]Video Export[/h1]

You can now export a 30s looped video of your map! This will greatly increase immersion as your players will be able to travel across flowing rivers, water wheels and forests full of gently swaying trees. Check out the video below for an example of a video export.

[previewyoutube=3Lg0W6b56kA;full][/previewyoutube]

 
Special Effects
A long-requested feature is the ability to add special effects to the maps. And now you can! Add fire, smoke, fireflies, necrotic fog or other exotic effects and really personalize your world. And of course, use video export afterwards to show them to your players in fully animated glory!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40663413/9cb563c099c6c9f88d5071380c190e7b43704565.jpg[/img]

 
[h1]Multiple Liquid Types[/h1]

Previously, only standard water was available in Dungeon Alchemist. No longer! We added frozen water, muddy water, lava and more! You can even combine them on the same map.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40663413/6758dbaf250f7f4c01bba3468708db3d5cfc2497.png[/img]


[h1]Customizable Abstract Objects[/h1]

We added a set of fully customisable abstract shapes, that allow you to add any texture to them. This is an easy way to create a wall that is not available yet, or that specific floor tile you really wanted. If you get creative, you could build entire rooms out of your own customised objects!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40663413/7cb1818994dc701e6b197562484e9d7aa2b8c3e0.png[/img]


[h1]AI Improvements[/h1]

We've been aware for a while that the AI was lacking in certain parts and could be greatly improved. So we spent a lot of time looking at its shortcomings and trying to remedy them. The AI is not perfect yet, but we do think it's improved greatly.

We rewrote almost every aspect of the AI-system, but these are some things you will immediately notice when generating a new room:

[list]
[*] Doors are placed more logically. They are centered when it makes sense, and doors will be larger for larger rooms. We also added logic to discern "front doors" and doors between interior rooms. 
[*] Windows are much less random and more symmetric. The type of window is also matched to the wall it spawns in for a more consistent look.
[*] Walls of adjacent rooms try to match each other. The outside wall of a building remains the same, even when the interior one changes. See-through walls such as dungeon cell walls now only spawn where they logically would, even when you place a dungeon cell inside of or next to an existing room. 
[*] Columns now only spawn for larger rooms and always spawn in a logical way relative to the room layout.
[*] Structured rooms such as chapels and throne rooms now generate in a much more appropriate way, resulting in far more structured, sensible room placements.
[*] Objects that should spawn logically in the center of the room will now do so. Same for objects that should spawn logically on the opposite side of the door, such as thrones.
[*] Objects that usually exist in a specific layout (for example, church benches) will now always spawn that way.
[*] Lots of subtle less noticeable improvements to the way objects spawn in relation to each other.
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40663413/fa061a0f204955be119eceb3d875cfeb6ad2af9e.jpg[/img]


[h1]Other Improvements[/h1]

There are quite a few other improvements in this update. You can always find all of them in the [b]Help > News[/b] screen in Dungeon Alchemist, but we'll summarize the most important ones here:

[list]
[*]A tooltip now appears when you draw a room to indicate how large the room is. You can also see the map size when hovering over the corners of the map.
[*]Added AI settings to the refresh button in the Select Room menu, allowing you to refresh only the objects, for example.
[*]Improved the search to show more relevant search results on top.
[*]We added a freely placeable version of every wall (previously, there was only one type).
[*]Improved the looks of the trees and added subtle animations to them. Especially the broadleaf trees received a considerable quality upgrade.
[/list]


[h1]So, What's Next?[/h1]

This update was postponed a few times because we underestimated the time it would take to overhaul the AI. We understand that this can be frustrating to people, but we've always tried to keep a high standard with regards to our updates. We only want to release a stable, fully featured update when it's completely finished. That's why we'd rather postpone an update than release a half-finished part of it.
We'll try to be more careful about announcing features too early for the next update, so that we won't have to postpone another update in the future.

When we're ready, we'll be announcing more info and sharing updates about our progress on our Discord, Reddit and Twitter account. Follow us there for weekly teasers, videos and awesome content!

[i]Yours in cartomancy,
The Dungeon Alchemist Team[/i]

notes.title: The Fata Morgana Update is live!
notes.notes:
If your next campaign takes place in the [b]desolate wastelands of the desert[/b], the [b]harsh beauty of the badlands[/b] or in a [b]bustling oasis outpost[/b], you're in luck, because we just released [b]2 new terrain types, 423 new objects and 10 AI categories[/b] that will suit your setting perfectly!

But that's not all. As usual, we have also added a bunch of new features and quality-of-life improvements to Dungeon Alchemist. Let's go over them now!

[previewyoutube=GiAgPn6yr14;full][/previewyoutube]


[h1]Steam Workshop[/h1]

We added support for [b]Steam Workshop[/b] to the app. Share your lovingly crafted maps with the whole world, and download the best work of other people to use in your campaigns! We have integrated the workshop completely in Dungeon Alchemist, allowing you to browse, publish and rate maps from within the app.

Pulling together a campaign or quickly finding an awesome map when your party wanders off *again* has never been easier!
 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40663413/e06a25fc5a88ff13e109e00cc0d6656f1a3c5346.jpg[/img]
 

[h1]Token Menu[/h1]

We have added a [b]Token Menu[/b]! You can now place tokens on your map and move them around. You get [b]15 free tokens[/b] courtesy of [url=https://www.heroforge.com/]Hero Forge[/url], and 5 more if you create a [b]free Hero Forge account[/b] and link it with Dungeon Alchemist. Once you link your account to Dungeon Alchemist, you can also [b]import your Hero Forge 3D digital miniatures[/b] straight into Dungeon Alchemist! It only takes a few seconds to set up, and you're good to go!
 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40663413/f9a04abee43cbbea67c7c7d44dad6ccdbfa5812e.jpg[/img]


[h1]Cinematic Mode/First Person View[/h1]

We have added two new ways to explore your maps and share them with the world.

The first one is [b]Cinematic Mode[/b] - just click the camera icon in the top right to activate it! Cinematic Mode allows you to fly around the map freely and take screenshots or record videos. This is a great and convenient way to make close-up images of your maps to show to your players during play, to give them a better idea of their environment.

Additionally, you can [b]dive into any token's point of view[/b] by clicking on the eye icon when you select it. This allows you to walk around the map as if you're in a first person shooter! Interact with objects such as doors and lights by clicking on them, and experience the art of Dungeon Alchemist as you've never seen it before!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40663413/8370d5fb43c71354128997d40fdee9f08c37b616.jpg[/img]
 

[h1]Recolor Objects[/h1]

Good ol' regular colours a bit too plain for you? Recolour hundreds of objects to create the look you want. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40663413/656ca9b2a490ed53babd1307608a24951e387bae.jpg[/img]


[h1]Quality-of-life Improvements[/h1]

We've added a lot of other stuff as well:

[list]
[*] Tons of object brushes that allow you to quickly paint pillows, candles, ruins, ...
[*] A hexagonal grid setting
[*] A strength slider for terrain brushes, so you can raise/lower/paint terrain faster
[*] A favourites system that allows you to record your favourite objects for reference later
[*] AI configuration options - you can now choose which parts of the room you want to have the AI generate
[*] A "Hide all UI"-button in the View menu, for when you want to have a fully immersive experience
[*] Get the name of an object by clicking on it and hovering over the Copy icon
[/list]


[h1]What's next?[/h1]

Phew, that was a lot! But of course, we're not done yet. Check out the News menu in the app (accessible from the top menu [i]Help > News[/i]) to read all the other changes and bugfixes.

As for our next update - we'll be giving the [b]AI a long-overdue overhaul[/b], and of course we'll be adding more objects and themes. If you want to be kept up to date on what's coming, [url=https://discord.com/invite/Wrrmb5YrJa]join our Discord[/url] for weekly updates!

Yours in cartomancy,
The Dungeon Alchemist Team

notes.title: Abandoned Ruins Update
notes.notes:
Hey everyone!

It's been 2 months since release, and we just launched our first free update! This update contains 462 new objects and a buttload of new features, as well as a jungle theme! You can find a full list of the changes in the News page in the app after updating, but in this post we'll highlight some of the coolest new things.

For starters, here's a trailer video:

[previewyoutube=H5SNyphSrFw;full][/previewyoutube]

[h1]Jungle Theme[/h1]

We already had forest and grasslands, but now we have added a third theme: jungle. Explore an ancient temple deep in the jungle, or discover an abandoned, overgrown town on the outskirts of civilization. Time to bring out your inner Indiana Jones!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40663413/53dbc13663c55d484fc3d4fcb313d10858e0b04e.jpg[/img]


[h1]Object Brushes[/h1]

A much requested feature, you can now paint families of objects on the terrain, allowing you to place down a forest in a matter of seconds. Alternatively, you could place down hundreds of pots and confuse the hell out of your players.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40663413/95942c5ca49fdc939f97a8140519e08ef14218a0.jpg[/img]


[h1]Stackable platforms with line-of-sight on export[/h1]

We added a bunch of stackable objects that allow you to get creative and build vertical structures. You can stack them, add lights to them, put stuff on them and they even export to your VTT with correct line-of-sight!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40663413/34464cafbfc590dbc574ca116c45cc47b2c47f11.jpg[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40663413/4e65598a3c3b45a358d5c7430d60702acf85d803.jpg[/img]


[h1]Free object placement and light customization[/h1]

You can now turn off collisions for objects, so you can place them freely wherever you want: in the walls, in trees, even in each other! And you can highlight your Frankenstein creation with haunting, weirdly colored lights. Time to get freaky!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40663413/aa6036c54149814e047805568d550e994991c2bf.jpg[/img]
 

[h1]Change terrain on the fly, expand maps freely, place rooms on mountaintops[/h1]

When you create a new map, you can now choose at which height you want your rooms to spawn, so you can now create an abandoned hovel on top of a mountain range. And if you're unhappy with the surroundings, just go to the terrain menu and generate another terrain on the fly! You can even expand the map now by dragging the corners of the map.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40663413/1a3418a92593a3beb33e6c9dbc544e2cf18ee6e9.jpg[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40663413/1a3418a92593a3beb33e6c9dbc544e2cf18ee6e9.jpg[/img]


[h1]Feature/theme/object suggestions on Upvoty[/h1]

We try to listen to the community as much as possible to gauge what your needs are and what things you are most looking forward to. To organize and structure community suggestions, we released [url=https://dungeonalchemist.upvoty.com/]an Upvoty board[/url] where people can vote for their most needed features and themes. We also moved our roadmap to Upvoty, so you can see what we're working on and what's coming up next.
Feel free to [url=https://dungeonalchemist.upvoty.com/]post your ideas for Dungeon Alchemist[/url]. We'll definitely be reading them!

[h1]What's next?[/h1]
We'll continue working on the [url=https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/1024146278/dungeon-alchemisttm]remaining stretch goals promised during our crowdfunding[/url] over the coming months. You can expect tons of new content and features soon! And just like this update, they'll be released for free to owners of Dungeon Alchemist.

In the meantime: if you like what we're doing, please tell your friends about Dungeon Alchemist and share your maps on Steam, Twitter, Facebook, Reddit, … We love to see your creations!

notes.title: v1.0.59: Release News & Hotfix
notes.notes:
Hi everyone! Welcome to all new users of Dungeon Alchemist, and welcome back to our beta testers. It's been a month since release, so time for an update on the state of Dungeon Alchemist!

[h1]Release Update[/h1]
Our release went great! We are currently rated "Very Positive" on Steam and we are seeing a ton of user-created content pop up on Twitter, YouTube and other channels. We even hit the top 5 of best selling apps on Steam for a few hours. It's so great to see people enjoying the thing we worked on so hard for over a year!

For the last couple of weeks, we prioritized answering support questions from our users and fixing a number of issues (mostly with Mac and Linux versions). With these out of the way, we're now back full-force on feature and content development.

"Abandoned Ruins" is the next big content update to look forward to, and we have a lot of other cool stuff in the pipeline as well. In the meantime, you can really help us by leaving a review if you like the app.

[h1]Staying Up To Date[/h1]
With our Kickstarter and Gamefound campaigns finished and the app released as Early Access on Steam, we are entering a new phase of development. We will no longer be communicating through Kickstarter and Gamefound, since we won't be reaching all of our users that way. Instead, the in-app news page will be the main source of communication with the community. We will also be posting these updates on our [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1588530/Dungeon_Alchemist/]Steam Page[/url], [url=https://www.dungeonalchemist.com/blog-1]website[/url] and [url=https://discord.com/invite/Wrrmb5YrJa]Discord server[/url].

[h1]Mac Performance Issues[/h1]
Some people contacted us regarding performance issues on Mac. This patch will greatly improve performance on your system, but if you are still struggling with running Dungeon Alchemist on your Mac, please follow these instructions:
[list]
[*] Lower the resolution to about 2/3 of the maximum using the [b]File > Settings[/b] menu.
[*] Set the Graphics Quality to Medium in the same menu.
[/list]

These changes, combined with the improved performance in this patch, should make Dungeon Alchemist run smoothly on most Macs from 2017 or newer.

[h1]Patch Notes[/h1]
[list]
[*] Improve performance on all devices by 20% or more.
[*] Improve performance on Macs even further.
[*] Fixed saving/exporting on Linux systems: the files are now saved with the correct extension.
[*] If you have a very low resolution and your UI scale is high, you could get stuck because the Settings window and File buttons are not clickable anymore. This is fixed now, and you should be able to always change the resolution again.
[*] Changed this news page to work on smaller resolutions.
[*] Fixed issue with people getting stuck halfway the tutorial.
[/list]

[h1]What's next?[/h1]

We're looking forward to sharing new content with you soon. If you're curious what's coming up next, you should join our [url=https://discord.com/invite/Wrrmb5YrJa]Discord server[/url] and check out the #official-content channel. We regularly post sneak previews of new content and features there.

In the meantime, enjoy Dungeon Alchemist!
